title: Path-Specific Causal Reasoning for Fairness-aware Cognitive Diagnosis

problem.claim: Cognitive diagnosis models need to predict students' proficiency while avoiding harmful effects from sensitive student information.

gap.claim: Existing cognitive diagnosis methods have not paid enough attention to the abuse of sensitive information and can be misled by shortcuts between inputs and predictions.

contributions.claim: A Path-Specific Causal Reasoning Framework uses causal reasoning to remove only shortcuts directly related to sensitive information while retaining useful information.
An encoder extracts embeddings for general and sensitive student information, and an attribute-oriented predictor decouples sensitive attributes.
A multi-factor constraint jointly addresses fairness and diagnosis performance.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the Path-Specific Causal Reasoning Framework and attribute-oriented predictor as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets, including PISA, are reported to demonstrate the effectiveness of PSCRF.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cognitive diagnosis predicts proficiency levels from student and exercise data and is important in intelligent education.
Limited interaction data motivates use of student information, but sensitive information creates social risks and shortcut-related fairness concerns.
The proposed framework retains useful sensitive-attribute information while eliminating sensitive-related shortcuts through causal reasoning and specialized prediction components.
The authors report effectiveness on real-world datasets such as PISA.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the fairness definitions, baselines, dataset details, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the causal assumptions or the exact form of the multi-factor constraint.
